selectionBasis: The 25 currently held lines tagged prioritize-distinct-teachable-owner-review in the exact prior third-100 screen; all remain hold-editorial at review time. This bounded cohort favors reusable expressions and includes collisions as control cases.
guardrails: A candidate owner is an authoring recommendation, not an approved lesson or release.
No existing-owner alias is approved solely from a metaphor or token overlap; source meaning and detector must match.
A one-time-image exclusion needs its own narrow source-specific evidence and register entry.
The six retained holds need source-form or owner-boundary resolution before authoring.

rows.exactGuideSentence: At work, you are expected to steer yourself.
rows.guideMeaning: Direct your own behaviour without detailed instruction; a driving metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Existing steer the ship (508) directs a shared undertaking; handing them the steering wheel (925) gives choice control. Neither is this self-direction sense.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Steer yourself without a destination or object is less idiomatic than steer yourself towards X or steer your own course. Check this exact source form and target boundary before modelling it.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The old system rewarded staying on the rails.
rows.guideMeaning: Following a fixed path without questioning it; a rail metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Going off the rails (851) means serious disorder, not necessarily a direct semantic opposite of rewarded conformity.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Staying on the rails can mean keeping a process functioning or following a fixed path. The guide chooses uncritical conformity, but the isolated sentence does not rule out the safer functioning sense; resolve before a keyed lesson.

rows.expression: stays in the hands of only a few people
rows.exactGuideSentence: Knowledge stays in the hands of only a few people without teaching.
rows.guideMeaning: Information remains controlled by a small group; a hand metaphor.
rows.candidateTarget: in the hands of only a few
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: In the right hands (533) concerns competence of custodians, not concentration of control among a small group.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The knowledge/teaching sentence makes control by a few people explicit. Teach the bounded control metaphor with a variable possessor and distinguish who holds information from who is qualified to hold it.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Digital communication is rewriting the rules of society.
rows.guideMeaning: Changing accepted ways of living; a writing metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Following the rules to bending them (680) and unwritten rules (954) concern compliance and conventions, not fundamentally changing those conventions.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Rewrite the rules is a reusable metaphor for changing accepted ways. Of society is the source domain, not a fixed part of the target; avoid promising every rule literally changes.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A flashy feature may dazzle people for a moment.
rows.guideMeaning: Impress briefly without lasting value; light is figurative.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: No earlier dazzle owner was found in the prior source-label inventory.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The advert-like feature context supports dazzle as impressing strongly. For a moment is a separate duration limit, not intrinsic to dazzle; teach this boundary in examples and distractors.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Public health has changed the fate of millions.
rows.guideMeaning: Altered the life prospects of many people; a strong natural collocation.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: No exact prior fate owner was found in the prior source-label inventory.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Change the fate of is a transferable high-impact collocation. Millions supplies source scale, not the target; examples need evidence of altered life prospects, not a trivial convenience.

rows.expression: every powerful tool casts a shadow
rows.exactGuideSentence: Every powerful tool casts a shadow when used carelessly.
rows.guideMeaning: Major benefits may have harmful side effects; a shadow metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Cast a shadow over the whole experience (1841) teaches a troubling event colouring an experience; casts a very large business shadow (781) teaches influence. The source uses an objectless warning about harmful effects.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The full every powerful tool aphorism is a tailored one-time image, while cast a shadow is a plausible reusable core. Resolve whether this is a distinct risk sense or can be linked to an existing owner; do not produce a duplicate shadow lesson or exclude the line yet.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Customers can place an order from their phones.
rows.guideMeaning: Submit a purchase request; a natural retail collocation.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: No matching prior retail order owner appears in the source-label inventory; bark orders (2071) is a different command sense.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Place an order is a standard reusable retail collocation supported by the phone-purchase source. Teach placing a purchase request, not receiving or delivering it.

rows.expression: cities pull people in like magnets
rows.exactGuideSentence: Large cities pull people in like magnets.
rows.guideMeaning: Urban opportunity attracts migrants; a magnet simile.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Existing pull people in the wrong direction (1910) concerns influence towards a bad choice, not attraction to a place.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Like a magnet is a familiar attraction comparison; cities and migrants are one grounded example. Teach the transferable attraction frame rather than a supposed literal force, and check plural/singular agreement in models.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The cities keep swelling as jobs concentrate there.
rows.guideMeaning: Urban populations continue growing; a bodily expansion metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: No earlier swell owner was found in the prior source-label inventory.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The jobs/population sentence supports swell as grow in size or number. Teach the figurative demographic use while keeping literal bodily swelling as a contrast.

rows.expression: quality of life begins to slide
rows.exactGuideSentence: If services fail, quality of life begins to slide.
rows.guideMeaning: Living standards start to worsen; sliding is figurative.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Slide down the list (1156) means a lower rank or priority, not a fall in living standards.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Service failure gives a clear cause for quality of life worsening. Teach slide as gradual deterioration with an appropriate subject; begins to marks onset, not certainty of total collapse.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A clever advert stirs desire for new products.
rows.guideMeaning: Creates a feeling of wanting something; a mixing metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: No earlier stir-desire owner appears; path from desire to purchase (1949) names a different sequence.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: An advert can stir desire, a reusable collocation meaning evoke wanting. Keep this separate from amplifying a desire that already exists at 3901.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The campaign succeeded by amplifying an existing desire.
rows.guideMeaning: Making a pre-existing wish stronger; a sound metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Stir desire at 3893 concerns creating or awakening interest; no earlier amplify owner appears.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The campaign strengthens an already present wish, rather than originating it. A lesson can teach amplify X figuratively with a clear pre-existing baseline and complete finite learner models.

rows.expression: built with speed in mind rather than clarity
rows.exactGuideSentence: The app was built with speed in mind rather than clarity.
rows.guideMeaning: Designed for quick use at the expense of ease of understanding; a natural spoken way to qualify or connect ideas.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: No prior with-X-in-mind owner appears in the source-label inventory.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The app was designed for speed, at a cost to clarity. With X in mind is a reusable design-purpose frame; rather than clarity is a source-specific trade-off, not an inherent meaning of the frame.

rows.expression: shared language that does not depend entirely on words
rows.exactGuideSentence: Football creates a shared language that does not depend entirely on words.
rows.guideMeaning: Common understanding through sport despite linguistic differences; a language metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Existing a social language (956) concerns social-value expression and speak the same emotional language (1577) concerns emotional mutual understanding; neither fixed target matches this cross-cultural sport sense.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Football enabling mutual understanding without common words supports a shared language as a conventional nonliteral common-ground phrase. Keep wordless understanding distinct from literal multilingual fluency.

rows.exactGuideSentence: After playing together, the distance between them often shrinks.
rows.guideMeaning: Cultural separation feels smaller; physical distance is figurative.
rows.candidateTarget: the distance between them often shrinks
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Mend small distances (1461) is a different repair action; this source describes a perceived gap decreasing after play.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The question explicitly asks how sport brings people from different countries closer. It anchors distance as cultural/social rather than physical; teach that context and do not infer total harmony from one game.

rows.expression: chase intensity for its own sake
rows.exactGuideSentence: Beginners should not chase intensity for its own sake.
rows.guideMeaning: Pursue harder exercise without a practical reason; chase is figurative.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Authority for its own sake (2068) is a fixed prior lesson about purposeless authority. Held source 4062 chases novelty for its own sake with a different object.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Chase intensity is exercise-specific while for its own sake is a broad frame. Resolve whether a new variable chase-X-for-its-own-sake owner would duplicate prior 2068 teaching or should absorb 4062; do not alias to authority without a reviewed sense/form expansion.

rows.expression: sport is a mirror of life
rows.exactGuideSentence: Sport is a mirror of life in a busy city.
rows.guideMeaning: Sports preferences reflect wider lifestyle patterns; a mirror metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: A small cultural mirror (960) already teaches a small practice reflecting wider group values, but its fixed target differs from sport is a mirror of life.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The sport/lifestyle comparison is plausible yet broad and tailored to a busy city. Decide whether a reusable mirror-of-X construction survives or whether this is one-time; check overlap with owner 960 before drafting.

rows.expression: a little workout for the brain
rows.exactGuideSentence: A puzzle is a little workout for the brain.
rows.guideMeaning: A small mental exercise; a body-training metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: No prior workout-for-the-brain owner appears in the prior catalogue. Sources 3989 and 3994 use different one-time gym comparisons and are not same-form aliases.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: A workout for the brain is a compact transferable fitness metaphor for an activity that exercises thinking. Little only marks scale. Teach actual cognitive practice rather than unsupported claims of intelligence gain.

rows.exactGuideSentence: The lessons come wrapped in colourful stories.
rows.guideMeaning: Are presented with an attractive outer form; a packaging metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Comes wrapped in convenience (404) uses the same wrapping verb frame but has a fixed convenience target and an ease-of-use sense; wrapped up with (1226) means closely connected.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Lessons wrapped in colourful stories describes an appealing presentation. A generic come wrapped in X owner may overlap 404; review whether canonical expansion is safe before creating a second lesson or aliasing this different complement to the current fixed detector.

rows.exactGuideSentence: At the professional level, the road narrows sharply.
rows.guideMeaning: The available route to success becomes more selective; a road metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: A narrower lane (750) concerns range of accepted styles, not selection pressure on a route to success.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: At professional level and few top athletes give the figurative selectivity context. Teach opportunity/pathway narrowing, not a literal road and not a guarantee that a named athlete will fail.

rows.exactGuideSentence: Without support, that early promise may never fully bloom.
rows.guideMeaning: Potential may never fully develop; a growth metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: Bloom in the morning (876) describes time-of-day energy; not potential developing. Other held bloom examples have different predicates.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Early promise denotes potential and may never fully bloom preserves uncertainty and need for support. Teach promise/potential blossoming as development, without converting may into certainty.

rows.exactGuideSentence: She spent Saturday hunting for a repair shop.
rows.guideMeaning: Searching actively for somewhere to repair an item; a hunting metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: A treasure hunt (704) is an activity or game, not the verb hunt for in a practical search.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Hunting for a repair shop is a natural figurative search use, with no actual animal chase. The object can vary; the lesson should preserve effortful searching rather than imply a guaranteed find.

rows.exactGuideSentence: A shopping list can be a snapshot of someone's priorities.
rows.guideMeaning: A quick revealing picture of what matters to someone; a camera metaphor.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: No earlier snapshot owner appears in the prior catalogue; a later held mental snapshot concerns memory, not a revealing view of priorities.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: The shopping-list example supports snapshot as a quick revealing view, not a literal photo or complete psychological profile. Keep the inference modest and evidence-based.

rows.exactGuideSentence: For some commuters, a phone feels like an extra limb.
rows.guideMeaning: So closely used that it seems part of the body; a simile.
rows.ownerAndAliasCheck: No earlier extra-limb owner appears in the prior catalogue.
rows.sourceSpecificReason: Phone use as an extra limb is a recognisable, transferable attachment simile for an object habitually close to a person. Teach dependence/constant presence, not physical anatomy or a proven addiction diagnosis.
